title: Partner without debt, use funds well, plan your next round

say: Partner without debt, use funds well, and plan your next round.
This is the video for module 3 of Accessing Grants, Loans and Partnerships.
A good partnership can do what a loan does, without interest or collateral. But selling to big buyers on credit creates a waiting period you must fund.

say: Getting money is half the job. How you use and report it decides whether you are ever funded again.

panel.heading: How you use money decides the next round
items: Partners can do what a loan does
Big buyers create a cash gap

Honest reports win the next round

say: Ada makes chin-chin in Port Harcourt. A supermarket chain offers to take 600 packs a month at 1,200 naira each, paid 30 days after the end of each delivery month.
Each pack costs her about 750 naira, so she makes 450 naira a pack, or 270,000 naira a month.
But she must spend 450,000 naira a month to produce them.
Because payment comes late, she funds about two months first: 900,000 naira. That waiting period is the cash gap.

She has only 300,000 saved. So her supplier gives 30-day credit, and she starts with two branches instead of three. Her cash need falls to about 350,000 naira, close to her savings. Partnerships, not a loan.
Write every partnership down. Name both sides, what each provides and when, prices and payment terms, who owns what, how long it lasts and how to end it, and signatures with dates.
Never hand over your recipe or customer list without clear terms. And anyone asking for a share of your business needs proper legal advice and registration with CAC.

panel.heading: What every agreement covers
items: Both names, exactly as registered
What each side provides, and when
Prices, payment terms, late payment
Who owns equipment, recipes, customers
How long it lasts and how to end it
Disputes, signatures and dates

say: Keep grant or loan money in a separate account, used only for that purpose.

say: Pay suppliers by transfer, so every payment shows on the statement. Keep cash payments rare.

say: Compare your plan with what you actually spent every week. And report problems early and plainly. A funder who hears about a delay from you reacts very differently from one who discovers it.

say: Bukola runs a catering business in Ilorin. She receives a 1,000,000 naira grant for a gas cooker, a chest freezer and hygiene training.
The cooker price rose between quote and purchase: 470,000 naira, 20,000 more than planned.
But the freezer cost 15,000 less and delivery 5,000 less, with training as planned.

The total is exactly 1,000,000 naira. Her agreement allows moves of up to 10% of a line, and 20,000 is about 4% of the cooker line, so she explains it in one line of her report. A bigger change would need written approval first.
Funded growth often brings equipment and new hands. If equipment uses gas, electricity or heat, have a qualified person install it.

cards.d: Gas, electricity or heat equipment is installed by a qualified person.
Keep a fire extinguisher where staff can reach it.
Show every worker how to switch off gas and power. Check their work daily for two weeks.

say: Train on safety first, and show every worker how to switch off the gas and power. Show, then watch, then check their work daily for the first two weeks. An accident hurts people first, and it also ends funding relationships.

say: For example, Ruth makes juice and zobo in Jos. She needs equipment costing about 850,000 naira. She mixes 200,000 of her own savings, a hotel deposit of about 150,000, and a 500,000 naira loan.

panel.heading: Ruth's plan to supply two hotels
items: Need: about ₦850,000 of equipment
Mix: savings, hotel deposit, ₦500,000 loan
Bad-month test passes
Days 1 to 30: NAFDAC, deposit in writing
Days 31 to 60: apply with the full pack
Days 61 to 90: buy, train, deliver, report

say: The payment is about 47,280 naira a month. Her worst recent month had 60,000 free, so the bad-month test passes.

say: To remember. Partnerships can replace a loan. Calculate the cash gap before saying yes to a big buyer. Write every deal down. Keep funded money separate, pay by transfer and keep receipts.
Report results in numbers, and problems early. And saying no to an offer that does not fit is a good decision.

items: Partnerships can replace a loan

Separate account, transfers, receipts
Report in numbers, and early
